doc.title: Lorraine Feather interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, March 22, 2023

title: Petula Clark in Las Vegas
summary: After giving up acting she got a Vegas job with Petula Clark, memorizing parts since she does not read music.

story.theme_name: Radio and television work: staff jobs, shows and broadcasts
story.community_name: Working with Sinatra: bands, Vegas and the Sands

blocks.x: I think we just did it by ear. The other gig I had in that period of time was with Petula Clark in Vegas. And somehow or other I got this job. Oh what happened was I had been waiting around for this acting audition for a showcase that paid nothing. There was a line around the block. And all of a sudden I just went, “I can’t take this anymore.” I had been singing in clubs a little bit, and I went home to my then-boyfriend and I said, “I’m not an actress anymore, okay? I’m a singer. I can’t take it, I just can’t. So I’ve been making some grocery money singing and I’m going to sing now.” So magically, a week or so later I got this awesome call to sing with Petula Clark in Vegas for a couple of weeks and wear beautiful outfits and be with an orchestra. But the thing is that they — one of the other singers who, “I don’t really have time to help you through the parts, I’m going to send you all the sheet music.” And I don’t read. I don’t read music at all. I could tell you what key something is in by looking at the sharps or flats, but I don’t read. So we got up there and there was a rehearsal and there was the orchestra and the two other women who’d been with Petula for ages, and I just followed along with them, like a millisecond behind the other singers until I’d memorized the parts. And Petula came up and said, “Oh you sound very good.” © Fillius Jazz Archive -5-

There’s one song of hers that just — I love so much, it’s called “I Couldn’t Live Without Your Love.” And I just — I guess it’s the chord progression or something. I appreciate arrangements. And you know she had good arrangements.
Yeah, she did. It was all top flight. I liked “Don’t Sleep in the Subway.”
